properties.name: An authenticating gateway in front — reflow2 has no authentication and is not getting any
properties.spec:
REQUIRED, declared 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word. reflow2 performs NO authentication and NO authorization, by design, and this node makes that a declared dependency rather than a caveat somebody has to find.

THE PUBLISHED IMAGE SAYS IT VERBATIM in its org.opencontainers.image.description label: "NO AUTHENTICATION — deploy on a private network behind a gateway that authenticates." `--http-allow-host` is Host-header allowlisting — DNS-rebinding protection, NOT auth, and reading it as auth is the mistake this node exists to prevent.

WHY IT IS reflow2'S DEPENDENCY RATHER THAN ITS OMISSION, and rule:no-foreclosure states the principle: reflow2 must never become the thing that decides who may read what. It delegates to an authority that already exists, on the stated principle that a server must not let anyone reach more than they could reach without it. Building an account system would foreclose that by making reflow2 the authority. So the absence is a POSITION, and the gateway is a contract the deployer owes.

flo2's reflow2_updates.md lists this among the two things reflow2 will NEVER do, stated once so nothing waits on them. Declaring it `required` is what turns that sentence into something the seam machinery can compute against — an unmet need on any deployment that has not supplied one, rather than a paragraph in a tracker.

SCOPE, stated so it is not over-read: this says an authenticating layer must exist in front. It says nothing about WHICH — flo2 uses Clerk (dec:stack-clerk); anyone else may use anything.
